editorial.marketOverview: For November 23–25, Nasdaq/QQQ retains a bearish, elevated-downside-risk baseline. The November 20 close showed broad liquidation with substantially worse semiconductor performance than the Nasdaq, an important sign of deteriorating leadership. No Sunday US cash session exists, so these are Friday observations, not live Sunday prices. The possibility of an oversold bounce does not yet outweigh the weak leadership and volatility regime.
editorial.whatChanged: Since the November 22 08:23 EST assessment, fresh Sunday market previews and QQQ valuation discussion mostly restate the Friday decline and the upcoming inflation and earnings calendar. The curated Open Watch file remains unchanged at 174 events, updated November 21 00:44 UTC. No verified new major catalyst or US market response warrants a bias change. Conflicting secondary Friday VIX close figures reinforce the need to verify the official series rather than promote a single unconfirmed reading.
editorial.marketInterpretation: QQQ and Nasdaq weakness alongside SOX underperformance and poor breadth indicate concentrated AI/semiconductor selling spreading to the broader tape. Falling Treasury yields could eventually ease discount-rate pressure, but a synchronized 10Y/2Y pair and current Fed pricing are missing. The earlier 29-basis-point curve estimate is stale. Previous Brent and WTI quotes are contract-unspecified and cannot establish current energy pressure. Fresh weekend commentary is an expected-impact discussion, not proof of a Monday move.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23: expect volatile price discovery, with 09:45 ET flash PMIs and SOX/SMH participation crucial to distinguishing a mechanical gap rebound from durable stabilization. Tuesday November 24: consumer confidence and Analog Devices/Dell earnings test cyclical demand and chip sentiment. Wednesday November 25: the scheduled PCE, GDP, durable-goods and claims releases may reprice rates and growth expectations; the Beige Book follows. All outcomes and market reactions are pending.
editorial.bullCase: After an unusually severe Friday selloff, a tradable rebound is plausible if QQQ rises with SOX/SMH, breadth becomes convincingly positive, and both VXN and VIX fall on verified synchronized observations. Better-than-feared PMI, inflation and hardware earnings could support that scenario, but these are conditional expectations, not reported outcomes.
editorial.bearCase: A failed early-week bounce, continuing SOX underperformance, poor breadth and persistent volatility would confirm elevated downside risk. Disappointing chip/hardware results, adverse inflation surprises or verified additional Nvidia regulatory developments could extend de-risking. No new such market response has been confirmed this Sunday.
editorial.watchNext: Verify Monday live synchronized QQQ/Nasdaq, SOX/SMH, breadth, VXN and VIX. Obtain official 10Y and 2Y yields with matching timestamps and correct percent/basis-point conversion, primary FedWatch probabilities and contract-matched Brent/WTI. Monitor Open Watch for newly curated primary-source catalysts, then track Monday PMI, Tuesday consumer confidence and earnings, and Wednesday PCE/GDP/Beige Book.
